guides.title: Using SoundCraft Help
guides.summary: How to find a page, move around help, and get help on the window you're looking at.
steps: Press {keys:Cmd+Shift+/} (the ? key with {keys:Cmd}) or choose {menu:help.open} to open help.
Point at a SoundCraft window, such as the Big Counter or Beat Detective, and press {keys:Cmd+Shift+/}: help opens on that window's page.
Contents lists every page by topic. Index lists them A to Z: type the first letters of a word to jump to it. Search finds pages by any word, menu name or shortcut, so typing Cmd+S finds Save Session.
Use the arrows at the top left, or {keys:Alt+Left} and {keys:Alt+Right} while the pointer is over help, to go back and forward.
On a command's page, Do it now runs the command just as its menu item would. When it's greyed out, the line under it says why.

guides.title: Start a session and save it
guides.summary: Make a new session, add tracks, and keep your work safe.
steps: Choose {menu:session.new} ({key:session.new}). Give the session a name and choose its sample rate, or start from the demo song to look around.
Add tracks with {menu:track.new} ({key:track.new}): choose how many, mono or stereo, and the kind of track (audio, MIDI, instrument, aux input and more).
Save with {menu:session.save} ({key:session.save}). The first save asks where to put the session. Later saves write to the same place.
To keep a separate version, use {menu:session.save_as} ({key:session.save_as}).
Open a saved session later with {menu:session.open} ({key:session.open}).

guides.title: Record audio
guides.summary: Set up a track, hear your input, and record a take.
steps: Add an audio track with {menu:track.new} if the session has none.
Click the track's R button, or select the track and press {key:mix.record_arm}, to arm it for recording.
To hear yourself through SoundCraft before recording, turn on input monitoring with the track's I button or {key:mix.input_monitor}.
Click in the timeline where recording should start, or select a range to record only that range.
Press {key:transport.record} or {keys:F12} to start recording. Press it again, or {keys:Space}, to stop.
To record several takes over the same range, select it and turn on {menu:options.loop_record} ({key:options.loop_record}) before you press record.

guides.title: Import audio files
guides.summary: Bring existing audio files into the session.
steps: Choose {menu:file.import_audio} ({key:file.import_audio}).
Type the file's path, or click Browse… in the desktop app to pick it.
Click OK. Each file goes on a new track, starting at the beginning of the session. Drag the clip with the Grabber tool ({keys:F8}) to move it.
Long files are decoded in the background, so you can keep working while they load.

guides.title: Cut, move and fade clips
guides.summary: The everyday edits: split a clip, remove part of it, move it and smooth the joins.
steps: Pick the Selector tool ({keys:F7}) and drag across a clip to select part of it.
Split the clip at the selection edges with {menu:edit.separate} ({key:edit.separate}).
Remove the selected audio with {menu:edit.clear} ({key:edit.clear}), or use {menu:edit.cut} ({key:edit.cut}) to keep a copy you can paste.

Pick the Grabber tool ({keys:F8}) to drag clips to a new place. The edit mode decides how they move: Slip ({keys:F2}) moves freely, Grid ({keys:F4}) snaps to the grid, Shuffle ({keys:F1}) closes up gaps.
Select across the place where two clips meet and choose {menu:edit.fades_create} ({key:edit.fades_create}) to add a crossfade. Select the start or end of a clip for a fade-in or fade-out.
Made a mistake? {menu:edit.undo} ({key:edit.undo}) undoes it, and {menu:window.undo_history} shows every change so you can go back several steps at once.

guides.title: Loop a section
guides.summary: Play part of the song over and over while you listen or work.
steps: Select the range you want to hear in the timeline.
Turn on {menu:options.loop_playback} ({key:options.loop_playback}).
Press {keys:Space}. Playback repeats the selection until you press {keys:Space} again.
With loop playback off, {keys:Space} plays the selection once and stops at its end.

guides.title: Mark places in the song
guides.summary: Drop markers on verses and choruses so you can find them again.
steps: Click in the timeline where the marker should go and press {keys:Enter}.
Select a range first and the marker remembers the whole selection.
Open {menu:window.memory_locations} ({key:window.memory_locations}) to see, rename and recall your markers.

guides.title: Export your mix
guides.summary: Render the finished mix to a single audio file.
steps: Select the range to export, or select nothing to export the whole session.
Choose {menu:file.bounce_mix} ({key:file.bounce_mix}).
Pick the file name, format and bit depth. Turn on normalize or dither if you need them.
SoundCraft renders the mix with a progress window, then reports the file's peak level and loudness (LUFS).

guides.title: Zoom and find your way around
guides.summary: Get the part of the session you need on screen.
steps: Press {keys:T} to zoom in and {keys:R} to zoom out, or use {key:view.zoom_in} and {key:view.zoom_out}.
Press {key:view.zoom_fit} to fit the whole session in the window, or {key:view.zoom_to_selection} to fill the window with the selection.
Press {keys:Home} to go back to the start and {keys:End} to go to the end.
Make quiet waveforms easier to see with {keys:Cmd+Alt+]}, and smaller again with {keys:Cmd+Alt+[}. This changes only the picture, not the sound.
Make the selected tracks taller or shorter with {keys:Ctrl+Up} and {keys:Ctrl+Down}.

guides.title: Keys: edit modes and tools
guides.summary: The function keys switch how clips move and which tool the mouse is.
keys: Shuffle mode: clips close up gaps when moved or deleted.
Spot mode: you type an exact time for a clip.
Grid mode: clips snap to the grid. Press F4 again to switch between Absolute and Relative Grid, unless Edit/Tool Mode Keyboard Lock is on.
Hold F4 while pressing F1–F3 (in either order) to turn on Snap to Grid in that mode.
The same as F1 to F4, for keyboards whose function keys do something else.
Steps through the modes in order: Shuffle, Slip, Spot, Grid.
Trim tool: drag a clip's edge to make it longer or shorter.
Selector tool: drag to select a range.
Grabber tool: drag clips to move them.
Scrubber tool: drag to hear the audio under the pointer.
Pencil tool: draw automation and MIDI notes.
steps: These keys work when you aren't typing in a text box.

guides.title: Keys: playing and recording
guides.summary: The keys that start, stop and move playback.
keys: Play, or stop if playing. With a selection, plays the selection.
Play at half speed and an octave lower.
Start recording on the armed tracks. Press again to stop.
Go to the start of the session.
Go to the end of the session.
Add a marker at the insertion point.
steps: These keys work when you aren't typing in a text box.

guides.title: Keys: nudge, grid and selection
guides.summary: Move clips and selections in small steps from the keyboard. These work in the Edit window.
keys: Nudge the selected clips or selection later by the Nudge value.
Make the Grid value one step larger or smaller.
Make the Nudge value one step larger or smaller.
Move the insertion point to the next clip edge. Add Shift to extend the selection.
Move the insertion point to the previous clip edge. Add Shift to extend the selection.
Make the selected tracks taller or shorter.
Turn the selected clips' gain up or down a step.

guides.title: Keys: Commands Keyboard Focus
guides.summary: Single-key editing: with Commands Focus on, letter keys run edit commands in the Edit window.
steps: Turn Commands Focus on or off with the a-z button at the right of the Edit window toolbar. It is lit while it's on.
The single keys work only in the Edit window, and not while you're typing in a text box. A key pressed together with {keys:Cmd} or any other modifier keeps its usual meaning.
keys: Trim the clip's start to the insertion point.
Trim the clip's end to the insertion point.
Fade in from the clip's start to the insertion point.
Fade out from the insertion point to the clip's end.
Separate the clip at the selection.
Nudge earlier or later by the Nudge value.
Nudge earlier or later by the next larger Nudge value.
Move the selection to the track above or below.
Extend the selection to the track above or below.
Go to the previous or next clip edge on the selected tracks.
Make the edit selection match the timeline selection.
Make the timeline selection match the edit selection.
Turn Insertion Follows Playback on or off.
Zoom Toggle: zoom in on the selection, press again to go back.
Zoom out and in (these work with Commands Focus off too).
